Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: A common fungal disease of apple leaves and fruit caused by Venturia inaequalis.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown circular spots on young leaves
Spots may become dark and cause leaves to yellow and fall
Dark scabby lesions may develop on fruit
causes: Wet spring weather and prolonged leaf moisture
prevention: Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves
recommended_action: Remove severely infected foliage and fruit
Use an appropriately labeled apple scab fungicide according to local recommendations and label directions

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that affects apple leaves, branches, and fruit.
symptoms: Small purple or brown spots on leaves
Leaves may develop circular brown lesions
Fruit develops dark sunken rotting areas
causes: Dead wood and infected plant debris
recommended_action: Prune infected wood well below visible symptoms
Remove infected fruit and plant debris
Use a labeled fungicide when appropriate

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease affecting apple leaves and fruit and requiring cedar or juniper hosts to complete its life cycle.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Orange or reddish lesions develop as the disease progresses
Small lesions may appear on fruit
causes: Spores moving between apple and cedar or juniper hosts
prevention: Remove nearby alternate hosts where practical
Plant resistant apple varieties when available
recommended_action: Remove severely affected leaves
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide according to local recommendations

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple
Apple___healthy.description: The apple leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Normal green leaf color
No significant spots or lesions
No unusual wilting or discoloration
prevention: Regularly inspect leaves for early symptoms
recommended_action: Continue normal crop care and monitoring

Blueberry___healthy.name: Healthy Blueberry
Blueberry___healthy.description: The blueberry leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green foliage
No significant leaf spots
No visible disease-related discoloration
recommended_action: Continue normal crop care and regular monitoring

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry Powdery Mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that produces a characteristic white powdery growth on cherry foliage and shoots.
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on leaves
Leaves may curl or become distorted
Young shoots may show stunted growth
recommended_action: Remove heavily infected leaves and shoots
Use a labeled powdery mildew treatment when necessary

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.name: Healthy Cherry
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: The cherry leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Normal green foliage
No visible powdery growth
No significant leaf spots or lesions
recommended_action: Continue normal crop care and monitoring

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal disease of maize that produces elongated gray lesions on leaves.
symptoms: Long narrow gray or tan lesions
Lesions may become rectangular and run parallel to leaf veins
Severe infection can cause extensive leaf death
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant varieties when available
recommended_action: Monitor fields regularly
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when disease pressure warrants treatment

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal disease that produces rust-colored pustules on maize leaves.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown rust pustules on leaves
Pustules may occur on both leaf surfaces
Severe infection can reduce green leaf area
recommended_action: Monitor disease progression
Use a labeled fungicide if economically justified

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease producing large elongated lesions on maize leaves.
symptoms: Long gray-green or tan cigar-shaped lesions
Lesions enlarge along leaf surfaces
Severe infections cause premature leaf death
recommended_action: Scout regularly during cool wet conditions
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when needed

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy Corn
Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The corn leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Uniform green leaf color
No significant lesions
No visible rust pustules
recommended_action: Continue normal crop management

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape Black Rot
Grape___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease affecting grape leaves, shoots, and fruit.
symptoms: Small brown or reddish leaf spots
Spots develop dark margins
Fruit becomes brown and eventually shrivels into black mummies
causes: Infected fruit mummies and plant debris
recommended_action: Prune and remove infected material
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when necessary

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Grape Esca Black Measles
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex grapevine disease associated with fungal pathogens that can affect leaves, shoots, and fruit.
symptoms: Interveinal yellowing or discoloration on leaves
Dark spotting may develop on berries
Severely affected vines may show sudden wilting or decline
causes: Stress and wounds that allow fungal colonization
prevention: Remove severely affected wood where appropriate
recommended_action: Remove and destroy severely diseased vine material
Consult local grape disease management guidance for affected vines

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Grape Leaf Blight
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal leaf disease that produces dark lesions and can cause premature leaf loss.
symptoms: Dark brown to black leaf spots
Spots may enlarge and merge
Affected leaves may yellow and drop
causes: Poor air circulation and prolonged leaf wetness
recommended_action: Remove heavily infected foliage
Use a labeled fungicide when appropriate

Grape___healthy.name: Healthy Grape
Grape___healthy.description: The grape leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Normal green foliage
No significant leaf spots
No obvious fungal growth
recommended_action: Continue normal vineyard management

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus Greening
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A serious bacterial disease of citrus that causes abnormal leaf coloration and gradual decline.
symptoms: Blotchy yellowing of leaves
Yellow shoots and reduced vigor
Fruit may remain small and develop uneven coloration
causes: Spread primarily by citrus psyllid vectors
prevention: Remove infected trees where required by local regulations
recommended_action: Contact local agricultural authorities or citrus specialists
Manage psyllid vectors according to local recommendations

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach Bacterial Spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease affecting peach leaves and fruit and producing characteristic dark lesions.
symptoms: Small dark spots on leaves
Leaf spots may develop yellow halos
Fruit may develop sunken dark lesions
recommended_action: Remove severely affected material when practical
Use only locally approved and properly labeled bacterial disease treatments

Peach___healthy.name: Healthy Peach
Peach___healthy.description: The peach leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Normal green leaf color
No significant bacterial spots
No unusual leaf distortion
recommended_action: Continue normal orchard care

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Pepper Bacterial Spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that produces spots on pepper leaves and may also affect fruit.
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots may develop yellow halos
Severe infection can cause leaf drop
recommended_action: Remove severely infected leaves
Improve airflow and reduce leaf wetness
Use locally labeled bacterial disease management products when appropriate

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Healthy Bell Pepper
Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green leaves
No significant spots
No visible bacterial lesions
recommended_action: Continue normal crop care

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease that commonly causes dark concentric leaf spots on potato plants.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on older leaves
Concentric rings creating a target-like pattern
Yellowing and premature leaf death
recommended_action: Remove severely affected foliage
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide according to local recommendations

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: A destructive disease of potato caused by an oomycete pathogen that spreads rapidly under cool wet conditions.
symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves
White fungal-like growth may appear under humid conditions
Rapid browning and collapse of foliage
causes: Infected seed tubers and plant debris
prevention: Remove volunteer potatoes and infected debris
recommended_action: Act quickly because late blight can spread rapidly
Remove severely infected plants where appropriate
Use locally recommended late-blight fungicides according to label directions

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato
Potato___healthy.description: The potato leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green foliage
No significant leaf lesions
No visible blight symptoms
recommended_action: Continue normal potato crop management

Raspberry___healthy.name: Healthy Raspberry
Raspberry___healthy.description: The raspberry leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Normal green foliage
No significant leaf spots
No visible disease lesions
recommended_action: Continue normal crop care and monitoring

Soybean___healthy.name: Healthy Soybean
Soybean___healthy.description: The soybean leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green leaflets
No significant spots or lesions
Normal leaf development
recommended_action: Continue normal soybean crop management

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash Powdery Mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that produces white powdery growth on squash leaves.
symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves
Affected leaves may yellow or become brown
Severe infection can reduce photosynthesis
recommended_action: Remove severely affected leaves
Use a labeled powdery mildew treatment when necessary

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal disease that produces dark spots and scorched areas on strawberry leaves.
symptoms: Small purple to dark red spots on leaves
Spots enlarge and develop brown centers
Severe leaves may appear scorched and dry
prevention: Remove infected leaves and plant debris
recommended_action: Remove severely infected foliage
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when disease pressure is high

Strawberry___healthy.name: Healthy Strawberry
Strawberry___healthy.description: The strawberry leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green leaves
No significant leaf spots
No visible fungal lesions
recommended_action: Continue normal strawberry crop care

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that causes small dark spots on tomato leaves, stems, and sometimes fruit.
symptoms: Small dark brown or black spots on leaves
Yellow halos may develop around spots
Severe infection can cause leaf yellowing and drop
recommended_action: Remove severely affected leaves
Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet
Use locally approved bacterial disease treatments according to label directions

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease that primarily affects older tomato leaves and produces characteristic target-like lesions.
symptoms: Brown to black spots on older lower leaves
Concentric rings create a target-like pattern
Leaves yellow, die, and may drop
causes: Infected crop residue and soil splash
prevention: Mulch around plants to reduce soil splash
Water at the plant base instead of wetting foliage
recommended_action: Remove infected foliage
Improve air circulation
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when necessary

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.description: A rapidly spreading disease that causes dark water-soaked lesions on tomato foliage.
symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves
Brown or black irregular patches expand rapidly
Severe infection causes rapid foliage collapse
causes: Water and wind-assisted spread of spores
recommended_action: Act quickly because the disease can spread rapidly
Remove severely infected plants where appropriate
Use locally recommended late-blight management products according to label directions

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease that primarily affects tomato leaves under humid conditions.
symptoms: Yellow patches develop on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to brown fuzzy growth appears on leaf undersides
Severe infection causes leaves to dry and fall
prevention: Remove infected leaves and plant debris
recommended_action: Remove affected leaves
Improve ventilation and reduce humidity
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when necessary

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A very common fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici targeting tomato foliage.
symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with gray or tan centers and dark brown margins
Tiny black specks called pycnidia may appear inside the spots
Lower leaves turn yellow, wither, and drop
causes: Rain or irrigation splashing spores onto lower foliage
prevention: Mulch around the plant base to reduce soil splash
Water at the plant base and avoid wetting foliage
Provide adequate spacing for air circulation
recommended_action: Remove infected leaves and plant debris
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide such as a copper-based product when necessary and follow the product label

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: A pest problem caused by tiny spider mites that feed on tomato leaf tissue and can cause extensive stippling.
symptoms: Numerous tiny yellow or white spots on leaves
Leaves may develop yellow or bronze discoloration
Fine webbing may appear on leaf undersides during severe infestations
prevention: Encourage beneficial predatory mites and insects where practical
recommended_action: Wash foliage with a suitable water spray when appropriate
Use an appropriately labeled miticide or insecticidal product if infestation is severe
Follow label directions carefully

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease that produces circular lesions with concentric rings on tomato leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Brown circular spots with concentric rings
Spots may enlarge and merge
Severe infection causes yellowing and leaf drop
recommended_action: Remove severely infected foliage
Reduce leaf wetness
Use an appropriately labeled fungicide when necessary

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease that causes severe leaf curling, yellowing, and stunted growth in tomato plants.
symptoms: Upward curling of young leaves
Yellowing along leaf margins
Stunted plants and reduced fruit production
recommended_action: Remove severely infected plants to reduce sources of infection
Manage whitefly vectors according to local recommendations
Use resistant varieties when available

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A viral disease that causes mosaic patterns and abnormal growth in tomato foliage.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
Leaf distortion or curling
Stunted plant growth and reduced fruit quality
causes: Spread through contaminated hands, tools, and plant material
prevention: Avoid handling healthy plants after infected plants
recommended_action: Remove infected plants
Clean and disinfect tools and hands
Do not save seed from infected plants

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato
Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato leaf appears healthy with no obvious disease or pest symptoms.
symptoms: Healthy green foliage
No significant spots or lesions
No abnormal curling, yellowing, or fungal growth
prevention: Regularly inspect leaves for disease and pest symptoms
recommended_action: Continue normal tomato crop care and monitoring
